verdict.rationale: Galileo documents its own threshold-based alert rules on log metrics. Each rule combines a metric, an aggregation function, a threshold and a time window, and fires automatically when conditions like high cost or rising hallucinations occur. The only documented action, though, is alerting, and the evidence does not show how alerts are delivered. Missing for 10: arbitrary triggered actions beyond alerts (e.g., running workflows, blocking, re-running evals), documented alert delivery channels or webhook targets, event types beyond metric thresholds, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Galileo enables you to get alerted whenever unexpected things happen.
Each alert configuration includes: a metric e.g. Cost, Correctness, Context Adherence; an aggregation function...; a threshold e.g. < 0.5; a time window e.g. 1 hour
Your cost is higher than expected, Your model is hallucinating more than you want
